subsystems.name: Precursor delivery
subsystems.role: brings the atoms or molecules to the surface, one species at a time.

subsystems.name: Ultra-high vacuum system
subsystems.role: keeps the surface clean so each atom lands where intended.

subsystems.name: Substrate and positioning
subsystems.role: holds and moves the workpiece with atomic-scale precision.

subsystems.name: Activation and patterning
subsystems.role: supplies energy to break bonds, or removes material selectively.

subsystems.name: In-situ metrology
subsystems.role: checks the structure as it is built, atom layer by atom layer.

subsystems.name: Assembly mechanism
subsystems.role: in the far vision, a tool that places individual atoms or molecules — today only a scanning probe tip can do this, one atom at a time.

buildSteps.title: Prepare an atomically flat substrate
buildSteps.detail: Clean and flatten a surface, often a crystal, so it has no steps or defects over the working area.

buildSteps.title: Establish ultra-high vacuum
buildSteps.detail: Pump the chamber to below 10⁻⁹ mbar so stray atoms do not contaminate the growing structure.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the first atomic layer
buildSteps.detail: Use molecular beam epitaxy to evaporate a material and let it land atom by atom, or atomic layer deposition with alternating gas pulses.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the layer
buildSteps.detail: Use a focused ion beam or electron beam lithography to remove or modify specific regions.

buildSteps.title: Repeat layer by layer
buildSteps.detail: Alternate deposition and patterning to build up a 3D structure, controlling thickness to single atomic layers.

buildSteps.title: Position individual atoms (for ultimate precision)
buildSteps.detail: Use a scanning tunneling microscope tip to pick up and place single atoms or molecules, one at a time, as demonstrated in research labs.

buildSteps.title: Anneal and activate
buildSteps.detail: Gently heat the structure to let atoms settle into perfect crystal positions.

buildSteps.title: Verify and finish
buildSteps.detail: Scan the finished structure with probe microscopy and connect it to the outside world.

prerequisites.why: already grows crystalline layers one atomic layer at a time for semiconductors and research.
deposits conformal films with atomic-layer control in industry.
single atoms have been moved and positioned in labs, but only serially and often at low temperature.
no known method builds macroscopic objects atom-by-atom at useful speed.
mechanosynthesis machines that build molecules piece by piece remain theoretical.

pathway.milestone: industrial thin-film growth by MBE and ALD
pathway.unlocks: atomic-layer control in coatings, electronics and optics.

pathway.milestone: deterministic placement of single dopant atoms in silicon
parallel, tip-based or self-assembled atomic patterning
pathway.unlocks: faster writing of atomically precise structures.
materials with theoretical maximum strength and custom atomic lattices — if the physics of mechanosynthesis can be realised.
